effective

/ih-FEK-tiv/ — rhymes with detective · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something effective successfully produces the result it was meant to achieve.

The new alarm proved effective: burglaries dropped by half.

Example

After implementing a new study method that breaks problems into smaller chunks, a student's test scores jump from C's to A's.

This study method is effective because it successfully produces the exact result it was designed to achieve. Effective is more precise than 'good' or 'helpful' because it specifically emphasizes that the strategy worked toward its intended goal.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

successful: Successful looks at the outcome as a whole: the plan reached its goal and things turned out well in the end. Effective looks at the tool or method itself — it works, producing the result it was designed for. An ad can be effective even when the launch around it fails.

efficient: Efficient is about the cost of getting there: an efficient method gets its results without wasting time, money, or effort. Effective only asks whether the intended result was produced at all. A treatment can be effective but slow and wasteful — working, yet far from efficient.

productive: Productive measures how much useful output something yields — a productive afternoon turns out lots of finished work. Effective measures whether the one intended result was achieved. A meeting is productive when plenty gets done, and effective when it accomplishes the specific thing it was called for.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

ineffective: failing to produce the result intended

futile: pointless; incapable of achieving anything at all

Where it sits · how big and lasting the results are — ineffective → powerful → effective → transformative

ineffective vs. effective: Ineffective is the bottom of this scale and the direct opposite of effective: an ineffective plan produces no result, while an effective one achieves its goal.

powerful vs. effective: Powerful is a step beyond effective: an effective remedy gets the job done, while a powerful one produces strong, dramatic results.

transformative vs. effective: Transformative is the strongest word here, far beyond effective: an effective program meets its goal, but a transformative one changes the whole situation permanently.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ef- (ex-)

Prefix — ef- (ex-): out, thoroughly (Latin)

Root — fect (facere)

Root — fect (facere): to do, to make (Latin)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending to; having the nature of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ef- (a form of ex-, 'out') + fect ('to do, make') + -ive ('tending to'): something effective literally 'works the result out' — it does what it was made to do, successfully producing the intended result.

Use the root in a new word: factory

Use the root in a new word: factory: A factory is a place where things are made — the same Latin root facere, 'to do or make,' hides inside effective, 'able to make the intended result happen.'

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Effective is the precise word when something achieves its intended purpose or goal. Use it for strategies, medicines, tools, or policies that work as designed. For everyday things that are simply nice or good, the plainer word usually fits better.
